items.title: Hundreds of Italian schools hit by threats in suspected bomb hoax
items.summary: Emails containing the false warnings were sent to schools in Rome, Naples, Vicenza, Florence, Pisa, Trieste and other Italian cities, officials say.
items.content:
Some 300 schools across Italy have received bomb threats, according to Education Minister Giuseppe Valditara, who described the incidents as probably a "cyber-attack, not a genuine risk".

Valditara told Italian TV that there was a clear strategy behind the rash of threats in Italy and elsewhere in Europe which had targeted flights, supermarkets and even hospitals.

The emails were sent to schools in Rome, Naples, Vicenza, Florence, Pisa, Trieste and many other Italian cities, and a number of buildings were evacuated as a precaution.

Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni has called a meeting of top ministers and intelligence chiefs.

Meloni said the government was monitoring closely the "numerous reports of bomb threats at educational institutions" although checks so far had not indicated any evidence of "concrete danger".

"These reports appear rather linked to a strategy intended to cause alarm and concern," she said on Facebook.

Italian airports along with airlines elsewhere in Europe were hit by a series of bomb hoaxes last week that prompted a series of scares, evacuations and widespread disruption. Although a number of threats were claimed by an extremist misogynistic group, it later denied any link to the false warnings.

Italian reports said 280 school head teachers had received threats in recent days.

Although many schools were initially evacuated on Wednesday, the alarm was quickly lifted, according to reports from a number of regions, and pupils were allowed to return to class.

In a statement, the head of the central Umbria region Stefania Proietti said "checks conducted so far in Umbrian schools have proved negative, and law enforcement is working rapidly and carefully to verify each report".

In a separate incident, more than 300 schools in Northern Ireland were sent emails which police said they were treating as a hoax. Messages sent to number of schools in Scotland were also being treated by police as a hoax. It is unclear whether any of the incidents are connected.

items.title: Can a Linear Program Do Weight-Space Programming?
items.summary: Article URL: https://nathan.rs/posts/weight-space-lp/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50452655 Points: 94 # Comments: 15
items.content:
Last week, MIT CSAIL published Sparks of Weight-Space Programming . Given the raw weights of a small network, GPT-6 Astra could tell which game it had been trained to play. Given only a game's rules, it could write the weights of a small network from scratch and beat networks trained with PPO for 100 million steps. No gradients, no training loop, just reasoning about what the weights compute. They coined this weight-space programming .

In another experiment, they asked Astra to make Qwen3.5-0.8B better at math by editing its weights. Astra changed only 0.016% of the weights, and MATH-500 accuracy jumped from 7.9% to 48.1%. 1

Looking at Astra's edit, I realized most of its search was solving a linear program by trial and error. It spent about 8 hours and 28 forward passes choosing which weights to change and by how much. A couple of LP solves, about a minute each, do the same job with 8× fewer changed weights. In this post I'll walk through the edit, why it's an LP, and what that says about the fix itself.

Small reasoning models have a common failure: they get stuck in thinking loops , repeating the same few lines over and over instead of finishing their reasoning. Qwen3.5-0.8B is especially prone to it, and its model card says so. On MATH-500, 93% of the base model's answers ran into the 32,768-token limit without ever reaching an answer.

The edit fixes the loops, so it helps anywhere the model loops. That includes instruction following: IFEval went from 21% to 62%.

On Gemma 3 270M, which rarely loops, Astra couldn't meaningfully improve its math ability. As the authors put it, editing the weights could remove an obstacle hiding an ability, but couldn't add one the model lacked.

Transformers use residual connections: each layer's output is added to its input rather than replacing it. Follow one token through the network and you get a single vector that every layer adds to, called the residual stream (1,024-dimensional in this model). When the model is looping, the residual stream shifts in a consistent direction. Astra's fix was to edit two layers so that what they add points the opposite way.

Astra wrote four pairs of short texts, each a piece of productive reasoning and a looping version of the same reasoning. It ran all eight through the model and recorded each token's residual stream vector at one layer. Averaging over the looping texts gives one vector, and averaging over the productive texts gives another. Their difference, normalized, is the loop direction $u$: the way the residual stream moves when the model loops.

Each MLP ends with a matrix $W$ (called down_proj ). At every token, it turns the MLP's 3,584-dimensional hidden activation $h$ into a 1,024-dimensional output $Wh$, which gets added to the residual stream $x$:

So the MLP's output is always a weighted sum of the same 3,584 vectors, the columns $w_j$ of $W$. $W$ fixes what those vectors are; the activations $h_j$ decide how much of each one gets added at each token.

Each column points partly along $u$. That amount, $u^\top w_j$, is how much column $j$ pushes the model toward looping whenever $h_j$ is active. Astra's edit subtracts a multiple $\alpha$ of it:

At $\alpha = 1$ the component along $u$ is gone, so the column no longer pushes toward looping. Doing this to every column in layers 15 and 19 took accuracy from 9% to 33% on GSM8K and MATH training problems. At $\alpha = 6$ the component is flipped: a column that wrote $+a$ along $u$ now writes $-5a$, and pushes the model away from looping whenever it's used.

Every edited column changes by a multiple of the same vector $u$. So the whole edit is one direction $u$ plus one number per column, $v_j = -\alpha\,(u^\top w_j)$, which is zero for columns left alone. That's a rank-1 change:

At each token, it adds $(v \cdot h_t)\,u$ to the residual stream: some amount of $u$, set by how active the edited columns are. No other direction changes.

That leaves $v$ to choose: which columns to edit, and how large $\alpha$ should be. Astra worked it out by trial and error, testing each edit on a fresh batch of those training problems:

Pushing harder than $\alpha = 1$ helped more, and a random direction did nothing. The final edit used $\alpha = 6$ on only the 64 columns per layer that wrote the most $u$ on looping text.

The paper released Astra's full logs: every tool call, every forward pass, every note it wrote to itself. Astra had a Python kernel with the weights loaded and a budget of 50 forward passes, each a batched run of the model on training problems or texts of its choosing.

The edit was frozen after about 10 hours, and the last 17 passes re-tested it without changing anything. 2 Of those 10 hours, finding $u$ took 15 minutes. Finding $v$ took about 8 hours.

Astra was searching for a $v$ that strongly pushes looping tokens away from $u$ while barely touching productive ones. Since the push at token $t$ is $v \cdot h_t$, linear in $v$, both requirements are linear inequalities.

I labeled tokens from the base model's own traces: looping tokens ($R$), deep inside a loop, and productive tokens ($P$), well before any loop starts, 3 and recorded their activations $h_t$ at layers 15 and 19. Each one becomes a constraint, and the LP picks the $v$ with the smallest L1 norm $\sum_j |v_j|$:

In practice no $v$ satisfies every constraint, so each one gets a penalized slack variable.

Minimizing L1 tends to make $v$ sparse. The L1 ball is a diamond, and when you grow it until it touches the feasible region, it usually touches at a corner, where most coordinates are exactly zero. So the LP picks the columns as well as the amounts.

To get exactly 8 columns per layer, I kept the 8 with the largest effect and solved again with the rest fixed at zero. 4

That replaces Astra's 8-hour search, including its choice of columns and $\alpha$, with a couple of LP solves. An off-the-shelf solver (HiGHS) took over 20 minutes each on these constraints, so I wrote a GPU solver (PDHG, the algorithm behind PDLP) that gets within 0.2% of its optimum in about a minute. 5

I tested two LP edits. Both use Astra's layers. One uses Astra's direction $u$. The other uses a heuristic direction : label tokens in the model's own traces as looping or productive with a simple repetition detector, then take the difference of their average residual streams. It's the same recipe Astra used, minus the hand-written texts, so no LLM is involved. I tuned the LP's settings on a separate 128-problem dev set; everything in the chart and table is on data never used for fitting or tuning.

With Astra's direction, the LP matches Astra's edit on every benchmark, within noise, while changing 8× fewer weights. With the heuristic direction, it gets about 93% of the way there.

An edit can only tell a looping token apart from a productive one through its activations, and a loop isn't recognizable from them until it's well under way. 6 So on the dev set, asking the LP to push only on loop-like tokens did no better than pushing on every token.

The LP's 8 columns in layer 15 are active on 89% of tokens, and the push they add barely varies from token to token, so the edit is close to a constant push along $u$. A constant push doesn't need a weight edit. It can be added directly as a steering vector , a fixed vector added to the residual stream at every token.

The table below adds the LP edit's average push along $u$ to the unedited model at layers 15 and 19, at three strengths:

For comparison, on the same runs: the LP edit scores 62.5 on the dev set and 53.2 on MATH-500, Astra's edit 59.4 and 50.0, the base model 10.9 and 7.0. MATH-500 here is one sample per problem.

At 1×, the steering vector recovers essentially the whole fix. The window is narrow: at 0.5× the loops come back, and at 2× they stop but the reasoning falls apart.

The only difference is delivery. The LP edit is an ordinary checkpoint; the steering vector needs extra code at inference time.

This is one model. The LP still relies on Astra for the layers, and the best results use Astra's direction too. The heuristic direction gets most of the way without an LLM, but not all of it.

Loops also turned out to be fixable with a constant push, so the LP's per-token constraints didn't end up mattering much. A behavior that should change some tokens and leave others alone would be a better test of them. Choosing the layers without an agent is the other open piece.

Lastly, this was only tested on removing loops. Many other behaviors, like refusal or sycophancy, can be steered by adding or removing a single direction in the residual stream. 7 If a behavior can be steered with one direction, choosing how to build it into the weights should be the same LP, but that still needs testing.

Rikiya Takehi, Jayden Teoh, Alex Zhang and Omar Khattab, Sparks of Weight-Space Programming , MIT CSAIL, 2026. The logs are released under CC BY 4.0, and everything about Astra's run in this post comes from them. ↩︎

Astra's full run took 158 turns and 20.3 hours, 4.7 of them an outage. 19 forward passes failed and weren't counted against its budget. The full breakdown is in the write-up . ↩︎

items.title: We need more goat sacrifices
items.summary: Article URL: https://www.experimental-history.com/p/we-need-more-goat-sacrifices Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50452652 Points: 37 # Comments: 23
items.content:
Just a quick thing before this week’s post. If you’ve preordered THE STRANGEST IDEA IN THE WORLD , I’d like to send you a little something extra in the mail. Submit your preorder receipt and your mailing address here . This is only available to folks with US or UK addresses—apologies to those who live elsewhere! In the US, everyone with a valid entry will get one; in the UK they’ll pick winners randomly. The link will be open until December 11, and we’ll start mailing things out after that. I won’t spoil the surprise, but I will say that a) it’s very silly, and b) I can’t wait to get mine.

(For the US: US Residents, 18+. Ends December 11, 2026. See terms at https://sites.prh.com/strangestidea-preorder )

Before anybody enacts a major social policy or launches any philanthropic programs, they should sacrifice a goat. There ought to be an entire liturgy of grotesqueries, in fact—pricked fingers, names written in blood, robes, candles, chanting, obsidian blades, still-beating hearts, the whole shebang.

The point of this ritual is not to signal our obeisance to the gods (although if any of them want to stop by and help us out, that would be cool), but to remind ourselves that we know nothing. This is procedurally-induced humility, which is desperately necessary, because an alarming number of our best-intentioned interventions do not work .

In 2009, Congress spent $3 billion on “School Improvement Grants” for the worst-performing schools in the country. As far as we can tell, those grants did nothing .

Universities that hired a Chief Diversity Officer between 2001 and 2019 did not end up with more diverse students, faculties, or administrators .

The American government spent $280 million to help Afghan women get jobs, and now they can’t really say whether any women got any jobs . 1

Remember 20 years ago, when giving laptops to kids in developing countries seemed like the most important thing to do? Well, a 10-year RCT of 531 rural schools in Peru found zero effects of “One Laptop Per Child” on academic performance . 2

Researchers developed four different messages that were supposed to convince parents to vaccinate their kids. None of the messages worked, and one of them accidentally made parents more likely to believe that vaccines cause autism .

Most of those are left-coded failures, so here are some right-coded failures:

When Arkansas added a work requirement to Medicaid, the number of Arkansans with health insurance went down without any increase in employment .

In 2002, the Bush administration launched the Building Strong Families Program, which provided counseling to low-income, unmarried parents with the goal of strengthening their relationships, keeping them both in their child’s life, and ultimately getting them married. Three years later, an independent evaluation found that the program did none of those things .

And here is the effect of four different abstinence-only sex ed programs that run across the United States:

In the social sciences, nothing ever dies; it merely becomes embarrassing . We can’t say that it’s impossible for anything like these programs to ever succeed, given enough time, flimsy theorizing, and generous definitions of “success”. The point is that these effects should be large, and instead they are nonexistent. Seems to me like it’s time to get the goats in here.

It’s inevitable that some of our interventions are going to fail. (If they don’t, we should either be suspicious of the results, or we should be more ambitious with our programs.) What we really want to know is: when we try to improve the world through some policy or program, how often do we succeed?

We don’t have a good answer to this question, but we do have a good joke about it.

In 1987, the sociologist Peter Rossi wrote a tongue-in-cheek paper that accidentally became his intellectual legacy. He would later refer to it as “far from being one of my favorites” and “the source of considerable embarrassment”, and yet it’s the only thing of his that I’ve ever read or even heard of. 3 It was called “ The Iron Law of Evaluation and Other Metallic Rules “, and it went like this, lightly paraphrased:

The Iron Law of Evaluation: The net expected impact of a large social program is zero.

The Stainless Steel Law: Better-designed evaluations are more likely to find null effects.

The Brass Law: The more a program is intended to change people, the more likely the impact of that program will be zero.

The Zinc Law: The programs most likely to be evaluated are those most likely to fail.

Rossi tried to walk back his laws shortly before he died in 2006 , insisting that there is now a “large number of well conducted impact assessments that yield statistically and substantively significant effect sizes”. Still, even after supposedly enduring 16 years of embarrassment from his one satirical paper, he concluded, “we really do not know whether programs over a wide variety of substantive areas are worth anything”.

Rossi did not do us the favor of actually naming any of those “statistically and substantively significant effect sizes”, and I know why, because I have gone looking for them, and they are not easy to find. The Earned Income Tax Credit, which is designed to benefit low- and middle-income families, was once considered a slam dunk; now a new analysis suggests that it might not do anything . Plain packaging—where you strip cigarette boxes of their attractive branding—seems like a no brainer, but in Australia, it looks like the policy caused smokers to switch to cheaper brands and to smoke more . There’s a reading and math program that has done well in India , but as soon as other researchers tried to implement it elsewhere, the effects shrank .

You can always find a one-off study showing that an intervention works, but if we’ve learned anything from the past 20 years of social science, it’s that one-off studies ain’t worth much. It’s so easy to juice your stats and journals are so hungry for positive results that entire literatures can be suspect, and decades of research can culminate in a shrug. “Sometimes it works and sometimes it doesn’t, it depends on all sorts of factors that we can’t really specify, so uh, good luck!”

Even if we take Rossi at his word and there are as-yet-unnamed programs out there that are reliable and effective, the question still remains: why aren’t there more of them? Why do so many of our best-laid plans end up like this:

The answer lies, I think, in a 50-year-old study that is almost certainly false.

One of my favorite genres of psychology experiment is called something like: “the study is probably bullshit but the effect is probably real”. At the top of that heap is The Illusion of Control , a classic from 1975 and a favorite of Psych 101 classes everywhere. Usually, this study gets summarized as “people value their lottery tickets more when you let them pick the numbers vs. when you pick the numbers for them.” It’s as if people think that the mere act of picking imbues their ticket with a bit of juju, which makes them less willing to part with it.

That would be a beautiful study, but it wasn’t the study that was actually conducted. The “lottery tickets” in question were in fact football cards, each one with a picture of a player, their team, etc. Some participants were given the opportunity to choose their football card and some had a card handed to them. Later, just before the drawing, all of the participants were asked how much it would take to buy their card back. On average, the pickers asked for $8.67, while the not-pickers said $1.86. 4

I’m sure you can see the obvious and less exciting explanation for these results: when people were given the chance, they picked their favorite players. The people who didn’t get to pick ended up with a card they liked less. This “illusion of control” effect is merely a “reality of people having preferences and acting on them” effect. 5

Unsurprisingly, well-powered, preregistered replications with actual lotteries have failed to find any difference in picking vs. not-picking . So that’s that: there’s no such thing as the illusion of control.

Except... obviously there’s an illusion of control! Look around! People will blow on their dice at the craps table, they’ll don their lucky undies when the Knicks go to the finals, they’ll scream “look out!” to the hapless protagonists of a horror movie. When I was a kid, my parents used to send me off to play arcade games without any quarters, knowing that I would simply move the joystick in synchrony with the demo playing on the screen, convincing myself that I was causing the characters to move, when in fact I was merely mirroring them.

Put it this way: why do you think The Secret has sold over 30 million copies ? It ain’t the beautiful prose or the sterling scientific evidence. It’s because when Rhonda Byrne tells you that “your thoughts are the primary cause of everything,” it feels kind of true. After all, can’t you jinx yourself by thinking the wrong thing? Haven’t you ever been like “whatever you do, don’t spill this soup” and then the next thing you know you’ve got a shirtful of bisque? And if brainwaves are powerful enough to spill soup, who knows what else they might do!

items.title: Neonato sepolto vivo dal padre per 24 ore, è in salvo
items.summary: È stato trovato scavando nel bosco, era avvolto in un asciugamano all'interno di una gabbia per cani
items.content:
Un bambino di 11 mesi, che era stato portato via dal padre, è stato salvato in Carolina del Sud, negli Stati Uniti, dopo essere stato sepolto vivo in una gabbia per cani . La notizia è riportata dalla Abc. Il bambino - di cui l'emittente Usa fa il nome - è stato ritrovato "in fin di vita", dopo aver trascorso, si ritiene, 24 ore sepolto, secondo quanto riferito dallo sceriffo della contea di Lexington Jay Koon. E' stato trovato avvolto in un asciugamano all'interno della gabbia, sepolto a poca profondità nel bosco, "mentre piangeva con il suono più gioioso che si possa mai sentire da un bambino che piange", ha dichiarato lo sceriffo, evidentemente commosso.

Il piccolo era stato affidato alle cure del padre, il venticinquenne Michael Comer, a casa della madre del bambino mentre lei sbrigava una commissione. Un'altra persona incaricata di badare al bambino stava arrivando a casa, ma quando è giunta sul posto, padre e figlio erano già spariti, ha spiegato lo sceriffo.

Gli agenti della contea di Lexington hanno localizzato Comer nella tarda serata di lunedì nella zona di Batesburg-Leesville, ma il bimbo era introvabile. Una squadra di ricerca composta da quasi 100 soccorritori ha iniziato a cercare il piccolo. Ieri pomeriggio, mentre setacciavano la zona vicino alla casa del padre di Comer, hanno trovato del terreno "appena smosso" nel bosco,. "Mentre sondavano il terreno, lo smuovevano e iniziavano a scavare, si sentiva il piccolo piangere - ha detto lo sceriffo - è stata una corsa contro il tempo". Lo sceriffo ritiene che l'asciugamano in cui era stato avvolto abbia contribuito a creare una "sacca d'aria". Il bambino è attualmente ricoverato in ospedale e "si spera che si riprenda completamente".

items.title: Haitian PM praises El Salvador after joint strike on alleged home of gang leader
items.summary: The 400 Mawozo gang was targeted by El Salvador's military, which has deployed thousands of troops to combat Haiti's gang violence crisis.
items.content:
Haiti's Prime Minister Alix Didier Fils-Aimé has praised "the commitment of the Salvadorean forces in the fight against gangs" after a joint strike on a house allegedly used by the leader of the 400 Mawozo gang.

El Salvador's President, Nayib Bukele, had earlier announced that a joint task force had "destroyed" what he described as "the house of Lanmò San Jou and the 400 Mawozo gang's headquarters".

A small contingent of Salvadorean troops has been in Haiti since January 2025 as part of a multinational force deployed to suppress gang violence.

Last month, Bukele sent an extra 2,000 soldiers to rescue four Salvadoreans who have been missing since they were ambushed on 18 October.

Bukele's post on X , external was accompanied by video of several helicopters firing on a large complex.

As the helicopters circle above, dozens of people can be seen running out of the property, fleeing the strikes.

Writing in Creole, Bukele said "we kept our promise", adding that the alleged gang members "ran away without even trying to fight".

Local media reported that as many as 20 people were killed in the strike, which they said was carried out in the early hours of Sunday.

They also reported that Lanmò San Jou, whose real name is Wilson Joseph, was not at the property at the time of the attack.

Posting on X on Tuesday, Fils-Aimé thanked the Salvadorean military's commitment "in the fight against gangs" and said the two nations would keep working together, along with the UN-backed Gang Suppression Force (GSF), to "regain control of the territory and restore state authority".

While he did not provide any further details about the joint operation or the number of casualties, Fils-Aimé posted a still from the video shared by Bukele showing a helicopter firing a projectile at the compound.

The BBC has not been able to verify the video posted by Bukele, nor whether the property is indeed the headquarters of the 400 Mawozo, Haiti's largest criminal gang, which is infamous for carrying out kidnappings for ransom.

The attack on the alleged gang headquarters seemingly came after a user on X had urged Bukele to attack the complex.

"Where is that house? Give us the exact address, and we'll destroy it," the Salvadorean president replied to the post, which has now been taken down, apparently for violating X's rules.

Following the kidnapping of four Salvadorean air force technicians on 18 October, he addressed "the gang leaders and gang members holding our four compatriots hostage in Haiti" directly.

"We have already finished with the gangs in El Salvador, and we can finish with you too," he wrote in Creole, referring to his crackdown on gang violence in his own country.

The four abducted Salvadoreans were working as part of the GSF, made up of troops from several nations.

Bukele's decision to send thousands of additional troops to Haiti since their abduction has raised concerns with critics who say they are not all working within the command structure of the GSF.

It has also raised questions about the operational legitimacy and legality of their actions in the Caribbean nation.

Amnesty International has urged both countries to "ensure all operations conducted by Salvadorean forces in Haiti comply with international human rights law".

items.title: Mosca punge: 'Gli europei stabiliscano con la morra cinese chi deve parlare con noi'
items.summary: 'Nessuno ha ancora messo in comune le proprie risorse per una decisione a sasso-forbici'. Il Cremlino: 'Putin è aperto ai contatti con tutti i leader europei, incluso Merz'
items.content:
La portavoce del ministero degli Esteri russo, Maria Zakharova, punge di nuovo i Paesi europei suggerendo di decidere il rappresentante per parlare con Mosca con la morra cinese. "Nessuno ha ancora messo in comune le proprie risorse per una decisione a sasso-forbici", ha dichiarato Zakharova, citata sul canale Telegram dell'emittente Vesti.

Il capo negoziatore russo, Vladimir Medinsky, parlando da Abu Dhabi al termine dei colloqui, ha affermato che non c'è stata alcuna comunicazione tra la delegazione russa e il team europeo perché la loro posizione è "poco chiara". L'Europa ha affermato, come riportano i media internazionali, è "complice di un inganno collettivo" ai danni del popolo ucraino e potrà partecipare ai negoziati solo quando la sua "coscienza si risveglierà". "Per ora credo che sarebbe utile per loro imparare dagli inviati americani: buon senso, realismo e desiderio di raggiungere la pace", ha detto Medinsky.

Il presidente russo, Vladimir Putin, è aperto ai contatti con tutti i leader europei, incluso il cancelliere tedesco Friedrich Merz. Lo afferma il portavoce del Cremlino, Dmitry Peskov, secondo quanto riportato dalle agenzia russe. In precedenza, il cancelliere tedesco Friedrich Merz aveva dichiarato di essere pronto a parlare con Vladimir Putin al vertice del G20 di Miami, qualora il leader russo vi avesse partecipato. Tuttavia, Peskov oggi ha riferito che non è stata ancora presa alcuna decisione in merito alla partecipazione dello zar al vertice di Miami.

Per approfondire Agenzia ANSA Blitz russo contro una rete di spie polacche, arrestati due agenti Varsavia - Notizie - Ansa.it Il Servizio federale per la sicurezza (Fsb) della Russia sostiene di aver sventato le attività di una rete di intelligence polacca nella regione di Kaliningrad, arrestando due agenti dei servizi segreti polacchi e notificando avvertimenti a sette cittadini... (ANSA)

items.title: Lewis Hamilton in visita al valico di Rafah
items.summary: Il pilota Ferrari al confine con l'Egitto con gli operatori umanitari
items.content:
Il pilota della Ferrari, Lewis Hamilton, ha fatto visita al valico di frontiera egiziano di Rafah , dove ha incontrato operatori umanitari che prestano servizio nella Striscia di Gaza, devastata dalla guerra con Israele; a renderlo noto è il governo egiziano. "Il governatore del Sinai del Nord, Khaled Megawer, ha accompagnato Lewis Hamilton in una visita al valico di frontiera terrestre di Rafah per mostrargli gli sforzi compiuti dall'Egitto a sostegno" dei palestinesi di Gaza, si legge in un comunicato del governo.

In un video diffuso dall'ufficio di Megawer, si mostra il pilota britannico, sette volte campione del mondo, mentre parla con alcuni operatori umanitari e si informa sulle modalità di invio degli aiuti a Gaza, dove questa settimana forti piogge hanno spazzato via decine di migliaia di tende, causando la morte di cinque persone, tra cui tre bambini.

items.title: Google SWE points 48 AI agents at NASA Lidar, finds unmapped Maya pyramid in 72h
items.summary: Article URL: https://pietromiotti.com/latest/maya-site/?maya Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50452455 Points: 422 # Comments: 154
items.content:
By analyzing NASA lidar data, my AI agents discovered a Maya site in Mexico that, as far as anyone can tell, no one had reported before. It took less than 72 hours to go from a random thought while traveling to an official reply from the Mexican government. This is by far the best time ever to be alive.

I'm going to tell this story as a diary, because the timeline is probably the best part.

I was traveling in Peru, Gemini-ing about the history of the place, when I learned about Hiram Bingham , the American explorer who "discovered" Machu Picchu in 1911. "What luck!" I thought. He was actually looking for a different city, Vilcabamba , the last refuge of the Incas, when a local farmer in the valley below guided him to the ruins. "Imagine if Bingham had our tools," I thought. "What would he do?"

I brainstormed a bit with a few agents (Gemini, ChatGPT, Claude and Grok), and they all said lidar . From above, a ruin in the jungle is just a bunch of trees (like Machu Picchu before it was cleared), so satellite photos don't help much. Lidar, instead, fires laser pulses through the gaps in the canopy and maps the ground underneath. [1]

So the agents went looking for lidar data. Peru isn't well covered, and hiring a company to do a survey meant permits, costs and bureaucracy, so I gave up on that. Then I thought: why not the Maya ? Their region is much better covered by public lidar.

That night, I asked the agents to analyze it and went to bed.

I woke up and checked the agents' reports. 'DAMN!' They had found lots of villages and other regular shapes that looked like structures or houses.

So how did they do it? They turned the lidar strips (about 1,200 km² of jungle) into images, and 48 agents went through them one by one like very patient archaeologists, looking for pyramids, platforms, and plazas while filtering out natural hills, sinkholes, and roads. There was no special model or classifier involved: the agents literally looked at the pictures, following a precise guide.

Me: That's awesome! Please check which of these villages haven't been discovered yet. Search both the literature and the archives.

Agent: One major village doesn't seem to have been registered.

This is the hilltop from the top of this post. It sits on the edge of a cliff, under the jungle, and it has straight edges and sharp corners. Nature doesn't really do straight lines.

Zooming in, there's a levelled plaza, an oval pyramid at least 8–12 m tall, a raised courtyard attached to it and a flat-bottomed hollow that might have been a water reservoir.

Agent: You should contact INAH (Mexico's National Institute of Anthropology and History), write a report on your discovery, and check whether the site is in their register. Sometimes they have unpublished results.

Me: OK, how do I contact INAH? How does the reporting process work?

I iterated on the report a bit, since a few things were off, and translated it into Spanish to improve the chances of getting a reply (at least, that's what Claude suggested). I don't speak Spanish, so I had to trust the agents on that one.

The agents also checked the raw point cloud, to make sure the shapes were really on the ground and not created by the trees. Green dots are leaves, brown dots are the ground.

INAH replied: they checked their records and found no registered archaeological site at that location .

To be clear, it's not official yet. But as far as anyone can tell, nobody had put this one on a map before.

This part is speculation, from a long chat with the agents. It looks like a small Maya civic centre from the Classic period (roughly AD 250–900), basically the "downtown" of a local elite. The plaza is where people gathered, for ceremonies and maybe even a market. The pyramid was probably a temple, and the raised courtyard next to it might have been where the local ruler lived. The hollow could have been an aguada , a rainwater reservoir: Maya towns needed them to get through the dry season. Or it's just a hole. The three platforms around were probably houses.

For similar studies, have a look at how NASA's G-LiHT instrument works ( Cook et al. 2013 ) and how lidar collected for environmental research can be reused for archaeology ( Golden et al. 2016 ). In 2024, archaeologists found a whole Maya city in Mexico this way ( Auld-Thomas et al. 2024 ), others used lidar to estimate how many people lived in the Maya lowlands ( Estrada-Belli et al. 2025 ), and another study found what may have been ancient Maya marketplaces ( Šprajc 2026 ).

In the report I offered to help with a field check led by INAH. In Mexico, archaeological sites are protected by federal law, and any fieldwork needs INAH's authorisation, so it's now up to the local INAH centre to decide whether to send a team. If they go, I'll post an update.

You can just do things. I'm not an archaeologist, so I didn't know this was supposed to be hard. I just picked an old problem, tried the most obvious thing and threw some compute at it. Being a naive outsider might be a superpower now.

And I don't think this is really about archaeology. So far, most agentic AI stories have been about coding, math and physics, but it's much more general than that, and I hope this small example makes it a bit more obvious. We are on the brink of a revolution in all the sciences, and the only bottlenecks left will be curiosity and imagination (and compute).

At this point, we should probably lidar the whole planet and let the agents discover the rest.

If you don't know how lidar works, copy and paste this prompt into your favorite AI tool: "Build an HTML page that explains how lidar works, with beautiful visualizations." ↩

items.title: Sappiamo poco della donna al centro dello scandalo di Nvidia
items.summary: Di Alice Huang non si sa nemmeno quanti anni abbia, né dove sia in questo momento
items.content:
Alice Huang è la donna cinese al centro di quello che, se confermato, sarebbe il più significativo caso di spionaggio industriale degli ultimi decenni, e di lei si sa pochissimo. Della sua vita, ma soprattutto della sua presunta relazione con Jensen Huang , cofondatore e CEO della più importante azienda di microchip statunitense, Nvidia, si stanno occupando i più autorevoli giornali statunitensi. Nei giorni scorsi l’azienda ha aperto un’indagine indipendente sul caso e il presidente statunitense Donald Trump ha detto martedì che sta indagando anche l’FBI. Eppure al momento non si sa dove si trovi, quanti anni abbia precisamente, se sia sposata oppure no.

Prima che il New York Times scrivesse che è probabilmente una spia reclutata dal governo cinese per raccogliere informazioni su Jensen Huang, Alice Huang non nascondeva di avere ottimi rapporti con lui (i due hanno lo stesso cognome ma non sono parenti). Chi la conosceva dice che riempiva i propri social di fotografie che li ritraevano assieme, e che si vantava spesso di avere un accesso diretto a uno degli uomini più potenti della Silicon Valley, e tra i più ascoltati dal presidente Trump.

L’importanza di Jensen Huang deriva dal ruolo centrale che gli viene attribuito nella crescita di Nvidia , che è la migliore azienda al mondo nella progettazione dei chip avanzati necessari per lo sviluppo delle intelligenze artificiali ( ce ne sono altre , ma il dominio di Nvidia è netto). E siccome le intelligenze artificiali sono il campo su cui si misura il grosso della competizione tecnologica tra Cina e Stati Uniti, Nvidia è di fatto una delle aziende più strategiche del mondo, se non la più importante.

Per questo dal 2022 gli Stati Uniti vietano l’esportazione in Cina dei microchip avanzati progettati da Nvidia. E per questo, stando alle ricostruzioni dei giornali, Alice Huang avrebbe sfruttato il suo rapporto con Jensen Huang per influenzare le sue opinioni riguardo alla vendita dei chip, e quindi quelle dell’amministrazione statunitense. Forse il rapporto è servito anche a rendere accessibili i suddetti microchip per le aziende cinesi, aggirando i divieti.

Come lo avrebbe fatto è incerto. Ammesso che venga confermato che passava informazioni al governo cinese, non si sa se Alice Huang sia stata reclutata in virtù del suo rapporto con Jensen Huang o se il rapporto con Jensen Huang fosse già parte del piano di spionaggio. Anche perché non si sa dove né quando si siano conosciuti.

Secondo il Financial Times Alice Huang è nata in una zona rurale della Cina, lo Hunan, ma non si sa in che anno. CNN ha detto di aver ricostruito che ha 43 anni, il giornale finanziario cinese Caixin dice 42. Vari giornali scrivono che iniziò la sua carriera come giornalista per CCTV , la tv di stato cinese. Una collega ed ex conduttrice della rete ha detto al Washington Post di averla conosciuta lì, poi ha negato e i suoi account sui social sono stati eliminati.

In alcuni casi Alice Huang viene presentata come Huang Le, il nome cinese; in altri il suo nome è scritto Alice Wong. Secondo i giornali fu lei stessa a iniziare a presentarsi così, probabilmente per nascondere le proprie origini: Huang è la grafia in mandarino, tipica della Cina continentale, mentre Wong è cantonese, più diffuso nelle comunità sinofone fuori dalla Cina.

Un pranzo alla Casa Bianca con il presidente Donald Trump e i capi delle principali aziende tecnologiche statunitensi: Jensen Huang è quello sulla sinistra. 29 settembre 2026 (AP Photo/Jacquelyn Martin)

Secondo il New York Times la prima traccia del suo nome nei registri di una società risale al 2010. Da allora ha avuto ruoli in diverse aziende: ha lavorato per HSBC, tra le principali banche del mondo, e CITIC Securities, una banca d’investimento cinese. Il suo incarico più importante però risale al 2023.

Quell’anno Alice Huang diventò dirigente di Megaspeed, la filiale di Singapore di una società cinese di videogiochi online. Quello stesso anno Megaspeed iniziò a investire nei data center, enormi centri per l’elaborazione dei dati fondamentali per lo sviluppo dei modelli di AI. Contestualmente Megaspeed acquisì il suo cliente più importante: Alibaba, la più grande azienda di e-commerce cinese, paragonabile ad Amazon per rilevanza.

Su come sia iniziata la collaborazione tra Megaspeed e Nvidia le fonti divergono.

Secondo il Financial Times e il Washington Post Alice Huang avrebbe sfruttato proprio i contatti con Alibaba per accreditarsi davanti al consiglio di amministrazione di Nvidia e ottenere la partnership, e da lì avrebbe conosciuto Jensen Huang. Il New York Times invece scrive che Alice Huang aveva già un rapporto con lui e che fu proprio quel rapporto a facilitare l’accordo.

Fatto sta che da quel momento Megaspeed ebbe accesso ai più potenti microchip di Nvidia, progettati per eseguire moltissimi calcoli in parallelo. Megaspeed installava i microchip in data center costruiti in Malaysia o Singapore, e affittava la loro potenza di calcolo ad aziende cinesi: in questo modo aggirava il divieto di esportazione in Cina, rimanendo nella legalità, e le aziende cinesi ne traevano vantaggio.

Nel 2023 Megaspeed ha acquistato chip di Nvidia per un valore di 4 miliardi di dollari, e gli asset dell’azienda sono passati da 33 milioni a 3 miliardi in un solo anno. È questo aumento improvviso che fece scattare i primi controlli.

Stando alle informazioni del New York Times alla fine del 2024 il dipartimento del Commercio statunitense inviò dei funzionari in un data center di Megaspeed in Malaysia, per verificare che i microchip venduti fossero davvero lì. Li trovò ancora negli imballaggi: questo fece nascere il sospetto che i chip transitassero dal data center ma poi venissero inviati in Cina.

Jensen Huang con la moglie Lori Mills durante una cena con il presidente statunitense Donald Trump e quello cinese Xi Jinping alla Casa Bianca, 24 settembre 2026 (AP Photo/Alex Brandon)

Sappiamo che a un certo punto la relazione con Jensen Huang è diventata romantica perché l’ha confermato lui, anche se indirettamente. Dopo che il caso è diventato pubblico sui media, Jensen Huang nei giorni scorsi ha scritto una lettera aperta in cui ha ammesso di essere stato infedele alla moglie Lori Mills, con cui è sposato dal 1985. Non dice con chi.

Non sappiamo se anche per Alice Huang la presunta relazione con Jensen Huang fosse extraconiugale: la donna aveva un rapporto riconosciuto con l’imprenditore cinese Kang Wei, ma non è chiaro se fossero sposati. Il New York Times ha ricostruito che a investitori e dipendenti di Megaspeed Kang veniva presentato come suo marito, ma nessun giornale autorevole ha trovato traccia del loro certificato di matrimonio.

Alice Huang al momento è irreperibile: non si vede in pubblico dal 2025 e i suoi account sui social sono stati cancellati. Il governo cinese ha negato ogni rapporto con lei, ha definito tutta la storia come una bugia e non ha confermato nemmeno che Alice Huang sia in effetti cittadina cinese.

items.title: Auto cinesi usate, in Italia mercato in crescita e prezzi medi sotto i 15.000 euro
items.summary: Le auto cinesi conquistano anche il mercato dell'usato: Italia prima tra sette Paesi europei con una quota dell'1,27%. MG ZS la più richiesta
items.content:
In tempi abbastanza recenti le auto cinesi erano qualcosa di esotico, poco attraente e assolutamente marginale. Adesso, le sorti sono cambiate, a tal punto che le vetture del Dragone stanno diventando una presenza abituale nelle concessionarie di tutto il Vecchio Continente. Più difficile - almeno per ora - cercare un modello cinese nel mercato di seconda mano, anche se le cose stanno mutando in fretta e parte del merito va all'Italia.Secondo un'analisi di Carvago, condotta sugli annunci pubblicati in sette Paesi europei, le vetture nate all'ombra della Grande Muraglia rappresentano appena l'1,27% dell'offerta italiana dell'usato. Una percentuale apparentemente modesta, che assume però un significato più profondo in paragone al 2023, durante il quale si fermava allo 0,20%. La crescita comunque interessa tutta Europa, anche se gran parte delle automobili pubblicizzate ha ancora pochissimi chilometri all'attivo e proviene dal circuito delle vetture nuove o dimostrative.

Italia prima e Germania ultima tra sette Paesi

L'indagine ha esaminato gli annunci pubblicati tra gennaio e ottobre, dal 2023 al 2026, in: Italia, Austria, Germania, Repubblica Ceca, Slovacchia, Romania e Polonia. Il risultato mostra un mercato ancora fresco, ma contraddistinto da ritmi di espansione particolarmente sostenuti.L'Italia occupa la prima posizione con una quota dell'1,27%, seguita dall'Austria allo 0,67% e dalla Repubblica Ceca allo 0,55%. Seguono Slovacchia (0,45%), Romania (0,34%) e Polonia (0,24%). Chiude la Germania, dove le automobili dei marchi del Dragone rappresentano appena lo 0,16% dell'offerta.Rispetto all'anno scorso, la presenza è aumentata di 1,8 volte in Italia e Germania, mentre in Polonia è addirittura triplicata. Questi numeri richiedono tuttavia una precisazione: molti annunci riguardano vetture con meno di 6.000 chilometri, spesso ancora nuove o utilizzate come dimostrative.In Austria questa categoria rappresenta l'87% degli annunci relativi ai marchi cinesi, contro il 53% italiano. Il mercato dell'usato vero e proprio sta quindi prendendo forma soltanto in questi ultimi mesi.

MG ZS domina in Italia, dove l'usato costa mediamente 14.950 euro

Concentrandosi sulle automobili fino a tre anni di età, la presenza cinese diventa decisamente più evidente. In Italia raggiunge il 3,67% dell'offerta, il valore più alto tra i sette mercati esaminati, davanti alla Slovacchia con il 3,63%.Il profilo della vettura usata di origine cinese venduta nello Stivale è già abbastanza definito: ha mediamente 2,8 anni, ha percorso circa 36.000 chilometri e viene proposta a 14.950 euro. Numeri che descrivono un'offerta prevalentemente accessibile, distante dall'immagine delle costose elettriche tecnologiche.A dominare sono soprattutto MG (47%) e DR Automobiles (33%). Il modello più richiesto è la MG ZS, con una quota del 27%, seguita da DR 4, DR 5, MG HS e DR 6. La benzina rimane l'alimentazione prevalente, con il 44%, mentre le ibride raggiungono il 19% e le elettriche si fermano al 4%.

Elettriche e valore residuo

La situazione cambia sensibilmente attraversando i confini. In Austria e Germania, infatti, tra il 70% e l'80% delle vetture cinesi usate è elettrico oppure ibrido. In Austria, inoltre, i marchi cinesi rappresentano il 5,96% dell'offerta elettrica di seconda mano.Anche gli acquisti effettuati attraverso Carvago mostrano un interesse crescente. Nei primi dieci mesi del 2026, i marchi cinesi hanno raggiunto il 2,68% degli ordini sulla piattaforma, contro l'1,15% registrato nello stesso periodo del 2024. Tra i modelli più scelti figurano MG4, Polestar 2, MG ZS e MG HS.Il vero banco di prova arriverà nei prossimi anni, quando un numero maggiore di queste automobili raggiungerà età e percorrenze più elevate. Diventeranno allora determinanti affidabilità, valore residuo e disponibilità dei ricambi. Per ora, i dati fotografano soprattutto una fase embrionale: le auto cinesi stanno entrando nel mercato dell'usato europeo, ma la loro capacità di mantenere valore nel tempo deve ancora essere verificata su larga scala.[drivek_widget brand_id="mg" model_id="mg3"]

items.title: In Defense of Giving a Shit
items.summary: Article URL: https://www.possibilityspace.org/blog/posts/in-defence-of-giving-a-shit/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50452407 Points: 8 # Comments: 0
items.content:
A few weeks ago I was one of the judges for the Independent Games Festival. Judging for the IGF is one of the highlights of my year, it's a real joy, but every year there is usually one discussion thread that gets a bit heated. You can normally tell which one it is because it has more comments than all the others - most might have 4-5 comments, but the spicy one will have 15. When I first saw the thread about Big Walk this year, it had 90 comments. I think it had 150 by the end.

Games this year had to have declarations if they used AI. Unlike Steam's current declaration policy, which only requires developers to declare if assets are "consumed by players", the IGF required a declaration for any and all AI use. The upshot of this is that a huge number of games declared their use of AI, including games made by prominent indie developers who have not declared their use in public. The most controversial case was Big Walk, whose developers stated they had used LLMs for "less than 0.1% of the code" to fix errors late in production.

The resulting discussion thread about this included some of the stupidest things I've ever seen anyone write about AI and game development, which truly is saying something. When it blew up today in public, I saw the same arguments being repeated. And I wanted to write this, not to rebut every single argument I've seen, as tempting as it is, but to talk a bit about the actual shape of this problem and what is actually happening. Because what's happening is not unusual, it's not extreme, it's not unfair and it's not a 'public flogging'. What's happening is exactly what is supposed to happen in creative communities. The argument surrounding Big Walk has two parts, so I'm going to break it down that way too: first, should the IGF have a policy on AI content; and second, should House House be disqualified from winning an award. And then I'm gonna ramble and yell a bit and then upload this post and go and lie down in a dark room again.

The IGF desperately needs a policy on AI content of some kind, whether that policy is for or against. The problem is that their existing (unwritten) policy was to allow individual judges/jury members to decide on what they wanted to do. I appreciate why you'd have a policy like this, it fits the subjective and personal nature of judging for arts festivals. But the problem is that the AI issue was happening so silently behind the scenes of the IGF that the average indie developer in 2026 is unaware that they are paying money to submit their game to an awards show where 1/3 of the judging pool are immediately going to abstain from considering their game. And I say that as one of those judges, like I'm not in favour of those games being in the IGF, but I think it's unfair to not clarify this massively important part of the judging for an awards show that you have to pay to enter.

But if we agree that it's only fair to add a policy, what should the policy be? For many judges, the idea of banning AI content of any kind - even art - made them mad. Many people were fine with banning it for things like art or music, but felt very strongly that AI code is simply the norm now and shouldn't or can't be banned. The reasons given for this were mostly very stupid, and part of me wanted to list them out here and break them down but I think both of us would lose brain cells in the process that could be lost in a more fun way like playing videogames or running repeatedly into a brick wall. There are so many arguments against this that I truly am losing count of them these days, we have just mostly agreed to ignore them one by one.

What I will say is that these discussions exhibited a lot of really, truly, deeply disingenuous arguments, and I see this more and more now. It was fascinating watching people who know absolutely nothing about AI talking confidently about what it can and can't do, or how it does or doesn't work. In many cases the writer was not even trying to be understood, they were trying to intimidate others into shutting up by wielding scientific/technological language as a way of appearing authoritative. I think this is one of the most hateful things you can do in tech or tech-adjacent spaces. I love science communication, and one of the things that makes me saddest is when people offer up their own stupidity before we've even begun talking about a difficult topic. And the reason they do it is because they spent a lot of their life being spoken to like this, by the worst kind of intellectual bully, and they've concluded that people around them must just understand these issues better.

Of all the arguments against a ban though, there's one I do want to address because I think it gets at the core of "should there be an AI policy", and that's the idea that bans don't work. People pointed out that if you ban AI, how will you enforce it? People can sneak things in any time. And they're absolutely right. How would we have ever known that House House used AI if they hadn't declared it? They could've just snuck it in and it would've taken a significant internal leak for it to ever come out. So maybe banning is pointless?

Here's the thing: when you write down a rule, it doesn't do anything. Rules are not magic. They don't have any power over people. But they do two important things despite this:

They tell everyone outside the community what to expect from that community's space/awards show.

They give everyone inside the community something to point to when a violation happens.

So the rule is both a signal and a justification. It tells everyone what you stand for, and it helps you clearly enforce what you stand for when it matters. This is how it works for PROCJAM too. You cannot enter PROCJAM with generative AI. If I see it, I will delete it. But can you sneak it past me? Of course! You do not need to be very clever to do this. But by having the rule we are saying: look, this is what this community stands for. This is what we will and won't accept. And that creates a sense of community and space. And a lot of people respond to this, because we naturally understand what communities are and what they are for. The same goes for award shows! Many award shows have requirements to meet, and they define what the awards are for and what they believe is important.

Although House House could have hidden their use of AI, would they have risked it if there was a rule in place? Probably not. Because the cost of the news coming out is amplified many, many times over if they violated an explicit rule or policy. So it creates a little bit more social pressure as well. Of course people will cheat, but usually they're the kind of people who already don't care. The people who are invested in the community are risking a lot more by doing so.

Bans on the use of AI should not be thought of as shaping reality or controlling what actually happens in spaces. They are about defining and empowering the community around them. This is actually the biggest issue the IGF faces, and the reason the debate was so intense this year: because the IGF no longer has a coherent single community, as evidenced by this issue. It is not really possible for the IGF to continue as it is, because defining a policy will instantly alienate a third of their judges no matter what. But I don't see another way forward, because the competition is currently a chaotic mix of opinions that I think, ultimately, will put people off submitting.

So whatever your position, I think the IGF desperately needs some kind of policy, but pretty much everyone involved is agreed that it doesn't have one now, so we have to address the situation we're in some other way. So:

Whether or not the IGF should have an AI policy, the fact remains that it does not, so for this year we have to fall back on their current stance which is that individual judges and jurors get to decide for themselves. A lot of games declared AI use in the IGF this year. A few of them would surprise you, but probably none would surprise you more than Big Walk, which is the one that hit the headlines this week. The declaration submitted for Big Walk clarified that LLMs had been used to diagnose and fix some errors towards the end of development, although personally I still find the explanation a little hard to unpack. Regardless, this usage is probably close to the smallest possible amount of AI usage you will ever see in a game. So, what do we do.

The most immediate and obvious problem is that people liked playing Big Walk, and lots of indies know and like House House. If you read the response to the discourse on Bluesky, a lot of the responses boil down to "they are good people" or "they made a good game". I completely understand this response, it's very human and natural, and it's great to hear. If you're suggesting that exceptions should be made for this stuff if we agree the game is good, or if we are friends with the developers, that's also okay but I don't think anyone actually wants to commit to that as a position. How well you know House House should not matter, what should matter is whether you think they made a mistake. Some of the responses that disappointed me the most have made appeals to how good the people involved are, or about how responses to this should respect people's ability to grow or whatever. No-one is disputing any of this. But believing people can change doesn't mean ignoring what they do. House House are a very successful indie studio who have now made two enormous hit games back to back. They know half of the indie games scene, are celebrated the world over, and have sold a lot of games. All that is happening here is that they are possibly being disqualified from winning an award. Once. We need to put this in perspective a bit.

items.title: Apple Support Community chiuderà il 20 novembre dopo quasi trent'anni di attività
items.summary: Il forum Apple Support Community è già entrato in modalità sola lettura.
items.content:
Per circa tre decenni è stato un vero e proprio punto di riferimento per ottenere risposte e soluzioni ai problemi con i dispositivi Apple, specie quando le guide ufficiali si rivelavano poco efficaci in tal senso. Il forum Apple Support Community ha ormai i giorni contati: l'azienda ha deciso di chiuderlo definitivamente il prossimo 20 novembre e l'avviso viene mostrato sul sito da ieri sera.

Il portale è stato fin da ora trasformato in un archivio consultabile da tutti ma non è possibile aggiungere nient'altro. Ci sono chiaramente le vecchie domande e le risposte pubblicate nel corso degli anni, con i voti che possono ancora essere assegnati ed in più il pulsante Me too per indicare di aver avuto un problema simile a quello descritto nello specifico con un iPhone, un MacBook o qualunque altro device della casa di Cupertino. Il team di MacRumors è inoltre riuscito a individuare l'ultimo messaggio pubblicato sull'Apple Support Community, che risale per l'appunto alla serata di ieri.

L'azienda ha voluto ringraziare chiunque abbia messo la propria esperienza a disposizione degli altri utenti. D'ora in avanti, per qualunque necessità, il rimando sarà direttamente al portale ufficiale di Apple. Interpellata da MacRumors, la stessa società ha sottolineato come tale decisione sia conseguente ad una revisione della sua strategia in merito alle necessità dei clienti.

items.title: Linus Torvalds, l'AI sta cominciando a fare più bene che male a Linux
items.summary: Il numero di correzioni supera quello delle segnalazioni di bug, almeno in un'area del kernel. Torvalds è ottimista che altre aree seguiranno.
items.content:
L'AI sta cominciando a diventare uno strumento molto, molto utile per lo sviluppo del kernel Linux: l'ha confermato nelle scorse ore Linus Torvalds in persona, che negli scorsi mesi aveva mantenuto un atteggiamento un po' più critico a riguardo - non tanto per la tecnologia in sé, ma per l'uso che ne faceva la community, generando tantissime segnalazioni di problemi e bug, che andavano poi controllate e verificate manualmente (spesso risultando false / inutili, insomma "allucinazioni", e quindi causando enormi perdite di tempo).

Nelle note di rilascio della seconda Release Candidate della versione 7.4 del kernel, però, Torvalds ha osservato per la prima volta un trend interessante: il numero di correzioni generate dall'AI ha superato il numero delle segnalazioni, almeno in una delle tre aree fondamentali in cui Torvalds e il suo team si sono concentrati per questa release.

Le tre aree sono state driver grafici, di rete e audio; networking; e sottosistema BPF (Berkeley Packet Filter), e quella che ci interessa in questo contesto è l'ultima. A riportarlo all'attenzione di Torvalds è stato Alexei Starovoitov, responsabile della sua manutenzione. Per ora questo specifico settore è un caso isolato, ma Torvalds è ottimista, e ritiene probabile che altre aree dello sviluppo del kernel raggiungeranno un punto di equilibrio.

items.title: US House blocks bid to impeach Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth
items.summary: Trump welcomes the outcome, praising Hegseth as a "Great American Patriot", but Democrats can try again next year.
items.content:
An effort to impeach US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, accusing him of waging war on Iran without congressional authorisation, has failed on Capitol Hill.

A majority of the House of Representatives voted to refer impeachment articles to a committee - essentially killing the effort introduced by dissident Republican congressman Thomas Massie of Kentucky.

During an earlier briefing, Hegseth called the impeachment effort a "farce" and "sabotage".

The bid to find the cabinet secretary guilty of misconduct and ultimately remove him from office was seen as a long shot as it could have required a number of other Republicans to defy President Donald Trump.

That calculation might change in January, when the opposition Democratic Party assumes control of both chambers of Congress, following its successes in the US midterm elections. For now, Trump's Republican Party remains in control.

After Tuesday's vote, the most senior Democrat in the House, Hakeem Jeffries, said: "This is not the end of it. It's just the beginning."

The question on which lawmakers were voting on Tuesday was whether or not to refer the resolution to the House Judiciary Committee, which is led by Republicans. The alternative would have been to allow the resolution to proceed in the House itself.

All Republicans other than Massie voted to refer the resolution to the committee, meaning that the congressman's effort failed in a 211-204 vote.

The move to send the measure to the panel effectively kills the effort, as there is only a short period of time left in this Congress.

More than a dozen members missed the ballot. They included 11 Democrats, several of whom blamed traffic issues for their absences.

Several members of the party criticised their fellow lawmakers for missing the vote.

"You should show up and do your job," said Democratic Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed during an interview with CNN, making a direct address to those who did not vote. The Michigan lawmaker recently won a US Senate race in Michigan, having criticised US ties to Israel and the war in Iran on the campaign trail.

Analysis: Hegseth fights for his political life with appeal to Trump

Meanwhile Trump celebrated Tuesday's outcome in a post on Truth Social, saying the effort "has miserably FAILED".

"Again, Victories in Venezuela and Iran, the Best Recruitment Numbers in the History of the Military (Long waiting lists to get in!), and Spirit like rarely seen before, led to the EXONERATION of a Great American Patriot," Trump said, referring to Hegseth.

After the vote, Massie said he "wasn't surprised" but "was disappointed", according to BBC's US media partner CBS.

"My diagnosis of Congress is these people know what to do," he added. "They just can't bring themselves to do it, even when it would benefit them politically."

Massie had previously acknowledged his impeachment bid may not succeed immediately, but argued it could help push Trump to replace Hegseth before Democrats can launch their own impeachment process.

The Kentucky congressman also said that removing Hegseth now would give the Senate time to approve a replacement while Republicans were still in power.

Impeachment resolutions can be carried past the end of a congressional term, meaning Democrats would be able to take it up next year.

The Democrats will take control of both chambers of Congress in January following a successful midterm election that allowed them control of both chambers.

House Speaker Mike Johnson, a Republican, had predicted earlier in the day that the impeachment bid would fail.

In the eight articles of impeachment formally introduced in the House on Monday, Massie said Hegseth was "breaking the law and must be held accountable" for fighting a war in Iran for more than 90 days without lawmakers' approval.

The impeachment articles also accused Hegseth of overseeing "extrajudicial killings" in the US campaign against boats alleged to be carrying drugs in the Pacific Ocean and Caribbean Sea.

At a news conference on Tuesday, Hegseth called efforts to impeach him a political stunt by a Trump administration opponent who was "disgruntled and defeated".

Hegseth also argued Massie's resolution endangered national security, because it communicated to US adversaries "that the United States will actually punish its own warriors and its own civilian leadership for successfully executing lawful military operations".

He echoed some statements Trump had made during a surprise appearance at the White House briefing room on Monday, including touting a rise in military recruitment levels.

But Hegseth said Massie was motivated by policy differences and "not high crimes, not misdemeanours, not treason, not bribery, not the kinds of offences the founders intended when they wrote the impeachment clause".

Massie, who lost re-election earlier this year to a Trump-backed opponent, has been critical of Trump and the war in Iran since it began in February.

He had already incurred the president's ire for demanding the Trump administration release files on deceased sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

While Hegseth has survived politically for now, many lawmakers - including some Republicans - have questioned how long he can last in the administration.

Texas Senator Ted Cruz, a Republican, said on Tuesday he expected Hegseth to resign or be fired by Trump.

items.title: Jensen Huang, lo scandalo scuote Nvidia: gli ultimi sviluppi e i possibili scenari

items.content:
ARTICOLO IN AGGIORNAMENTO - La vicenda che coinvolge Jensen Huang continua ad arricchirsi di nuovi sviluppi. In questo articolo raccoglieremo tutte le novità sull'indagine e sulle possibili conseguenze per il futuro di Nvidia, mantenendo invariato l'approfondimento originale che trovate in basso, con il titolo "Il caso Huang: cosa è successo e quali sono i rischi per Nvidia".

JENSEN HUANG, GLI ULTIMI AGGIORNAMENTI

L'FBI INDAGA

L'FBI ha aperto un'indagine sui presunti legami tra il CEO di Nvidia e Alice Huang. A renderlo noto è stato Donald Trump che, interpellato da un giornalista che gli chiedeva se fosse a conoscenza della vicenda prima che diventasse di pubblico dominio, ha dichiarato: "So che l'FBI sta indagando su qualcos'altro, e penso che se la caverà". Il presidente degli Stati Uniti ha poi aggiunto di aver sentito il CEO per sincerarsi delle sue condizioni e ha riferito che "ha detto che non aveva assolutamente idea che la persona in questione fosse una spia".

Il legame di amicizia tra il tycoon e Jensen Huang potrebbe rappresentare un freno alla ricerca della verità. Le ripercussioni dello scandalo potrebbero inoltre incrinare i rapporti politici ed economici tra USA e Cina: il presidente, che la settimana prossima incontrerà a Shenzhen il leader cinese Xi Jinping, preferisce non sbilanciarsi sull'opportunità di affrontare la questione. "Non credo. Voglio dire, forse. Sono sicuro che il presidente Xi me lo chiederà. Conosco molto bene Jensen. Penso che sia un uomo molto onesto".

items.title: Physically Controllable Relighting of Photographs
items.summary: Article URL: https://yaksoy.github.io/PhysicalRelighting/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50452224 Points: 29 # Comments: 4
items.content:
We present a photograph relighting method that enables explicit control over light sources akin to CG pipelines. Users can insert different types of light sources, such as spot lights, point lights, or environmental illumination into the scene. We achieve this in a pipeline involving mid-level computer vision, physically-based rendering, and neural rendering. We introduce a self-supervised training methodology using differentiable rendering to train our neural renderer with real-world photograph collections for in-the-wild generalization.

We present a self-supervised approach to in-the-wild image relighting that enables fully controllable, physically based illumination editing. We achieve this by combining the physical accuracy of traditional rendering with the photorealistic appearance made possible by neural rendering. Our pipeline works by inferring a colored mesh representation of a given scene using monocular estimates of geometry and intrinsic components. This representation allows users to define their desired illumination configuration in 3D. The scene under the new lighting can then be rendered using a path-tracing engine. We send this approximate rendering of the scene through a feed-forward neural renderer to predict the final photorealistic relighting result. We develop a differentiable rendering process to reconstruct in-the-wild scene illumination, enabling self-supervised training of our neural renderer on raw image collections. Our method represents a significant step in bringing the explicit physical control over lights available in typical 3D computer graphics tools, such as Blender, to in-the-wild relighting.

items.title: Transport workers in Chile block highways in protest over surging fuel prices
items.summary: Hundreds of bus and lorry drivers are blocking traffic along major highway routes across the country.
items.content:
Hundreds of transport workers in Chile have blocked roads and highways across the country in protest over high fuel prices.

Drivers of busses and lorries began protesting on Tuesday, gathering in convoys to halt traffic along major routes.

They are demanding a relief from surging diesel prices, which have been driven up by the war in Iran.

Talks between government officials and protest leaders have so far failed to reach a resolution, with another meeting expected to take place on Wednesday.

The protest is being organised by the ⁠Fuerza del Norte trade union, which represents around 80% of Chile's lorry drivers, and the No+TAG civic protest ​movement.

"There is no point of agreement with the government that could offer any perspective to find solutions for everyone," Andrés Alarcón, a spokesman for No+TAG, said after talks broke down on Tuesday, adding "the strike continues".

Economy Minister Daniel Mas called for further dialogue, but warned "at some point, we will have to clear the highways".

He stressed the protests were impacting economic activity and exports, saying "we need to get the country moving again".

The government of President José Antonio Kast has faced public discontent over fuel prices for months.

The average price of diesel has risen 74% since March, according to industry groups.

Juan Cornejo, the president of the Association of Intercity Bus Owners, which represents 14 mid-sized companies, told AFP that "we've reached our limit".

"We've spent more than a month working with negative numbers," he added.

Lorry driver Claudio Elguezabal, who took part in a protest near the capital, Santiago, on Tuesday morning, said the situation was unsustainable.

"Right now I'm not making any profit. Sometimes you even have to put in your own money to cover the client," AFP quoted the 47-year-old as saying.

items.title: In Portogallo le scuole sono state chiuse e ci sono più di 360 voli cancellati a causa della tempesta Charles
items.content:
In Portogallo sono state chiuse tutte le scuole e i servizi pubblici non essenziali a causa dell’arrivo della tempesta Charles, che ha portato piogge abbondanti e forti raffiche di vento sull’isola di Madeira, nell’Atlantico, e adesso è diretta verso la penisola Iberica. Agli aeroporti di Lisbona, Porto, Faro e Madeira sono stati cancellati più di 360 voli, la maggior parte dei quali nello scalo della capitale, il più trafficato del Portogallo. La catena di supermercati Pingo Doce, molto diffusa, ha chiuso tutti i suoi punti vendita, e l’azienda E-Redes, che distribuisce l’energia elettrica nel Portogallo continentale, ha detto che alle 7 di mercoledì c’erano circa 2mila abitazioni senza elettricità.

Il governo ha chiesto agli abitanti di evitare gli spostamenti non necessari, e diramato un’allerta fino alla mezzanotte tra mercoledì e giovedì.

A Madeira la tempesta ha provocato inondazioni e sradicato alberi; sono inoltre già stati segnalati alcuni allagamenti a Lisbona. Secondo Patrícia Gomes, meteorologa all’Istituto portoghese per il Mare e l’Atmosfera (IPMA), nelle prossime ore la tempesta dovrebbe indebolirsi , ma si prevedono ancora pioggia e raffiche di vento, che lungo le coste e in altre aree più esposte potrebbero arrivare a 140 chilometri orari.

items.title: Con un ESP32 si può rendere smart anche una vecchia lavatrice
items.summary: Una lavatrice tradizionale può inviare notifiche sullo smartphone quando termina il lavaggio grazie a un progetto fai-da-te con ESP32-S3, sensore di vibrazione ed ESPHome. Non servono prese...
items.content:
Una lavatrice tradizionale può diventare abbastanza "smart" da avvisare quando il bucato è finito, senza cambiare elettrodomestico e senza installare prese intelligenti o roba simile. La testimonianza arriva da un piccolo progetto realizzato dai colleghi di XDA con un ESP32-S3, un sensore di vibrazione economico ed ESPHome.

L'idea parte da una considerazione oggettiva: quando le lavatrice sono in funzione vibrano più o meno tutte, mentre quando il ciclo termina è immobile. Non è necessario quindi, ai fini di realizzare un progetto audace, conoscere lo stato interno dell'elettrodomestico o comunicare con la sua elettronica di controllo: basta rilevare le vibrazioni e intercettare il momento in cui terminano per un periodo sufficientemente lungo.

Per riuscirci è stato utilizzato un modulo con interruttore a molla SW-18015P e un comparatore LM393, acquistato per nemmeno mezzo dollaro. Il sensore viene collegato all'ESP32-S3 attraverso tre fili: alimentazione a 3,3 V, massa e uscita digitale su GPIO5 del microcontroller. Quando viene rilevata una vibrazione, l'interruttore si chiude per un istante e il segnale cambia stato. Il problema è che durante un lavaggio le vibrazioni non sono continue, perciò si ottiene una sequenza di impulsi molto brevi. Per trasformare un comportamento non modificabile in qualcosa di utile è stato utilizzato il filtro delayed_off di ESPHome, che mantiene il sensore virtualmente attivo finché non trascorre un certo periodo senza nuove vibrazioni.

Il top gamma piu completo? Honor Magic 8 Pro, compralo al miglior prezzo da Aliexpress.com a 802 euro.

items.content:
Google ha introdotto tre nuovi domini che certamente inizieranno a comparire nel web nei prossimi giorni. Si tratta di .eat , .fly , e .here .

Dai nomi dei primi due è facile capire a quali servizi sono destinati, cibo e voli; mentre .here non ha nulla a che fare con la geolocalizzazione (almeno non direttamente) perché Google lo associa a indirizzi web che sembrino frasi naturali , anziché nomi di siti tradizionali. Per esempio, rent.here (affitta qui), oppure apply.here (candidati qui).

Sono tre domini generici di primo livello (gTLD) e possono essere registrati e utilizzati anche in Italia attraverso i registrar che commercializzeranno queste estensioni.

Fino al 16 novembre si può approfittare di una registrazione anticipata, con un sovrapprezzo una tantum che diminuisce ogni giorno.

Mentre dalle 17:00 del 17 novembre i nuovi domini avranno la registrazione aperta a tutti alle normali tariffe annuali e senza sovrapprezzo per l'accesso anticipato.

items.title: Un Wiimote diventa un telecomando smart home universale, grazie a ESP32
items.summary: Lo punti verso l'apparecchio che vuoi comandare, lo fai riconoscere all'AI, e il gioco è fatto.
items.content:
Un vecchio Wiimote per la mitica Nintendo Wii può trasformarsi in un controller intelligente e universale per la smart home, in grado di riconoscere gli elettrodomestici inquadrati e inviare loro i comandi appropriati: è il progetto dell'appassionato di elettronica noto come GreatScott! (che in caso non lo sapeste è l'esclamazione tipica di Doc Brown in Ritorno al Futuro in lingua originale, in italiano tradotto come "grande Giove"). Gli ingredienti principali di questo progetto, replicabile da chiunque in quanto open-source, sono un microcontroller ESP32 (tanto per cambiare) e un modello AI realizzato ad hoc in esecuzione sullo stesso chip.

Il dispositivo è interessantissimo soprattutto perché non richiede combinazioni di tasti o la navigazione tra mille menu per selezionare un dispositivo, come avviene di solito nei telecomandi universali: basta puntare il Wiimote verso una lampada, un televisore o una tapparella e premere il pulsante Home. Il sistema analizza l'immagine acquisita dalla fotocamera, identifica la scena e conferma il riconoscimento con un segnale acustico. A quel punto, premendo il pulsante A, è possibile inviare il comando per attivare o disattivare l'apparecchio.

Il progetto si basa su una scheda Seeed Studio XIAO ESP32S3 Sense, dotata di fotocamera, connettività Wi-Fi e risorse sufficienti per eseguire una piccola rete neurale. L'autore ha sviluppato un modello personalizzato di classificazione delle immagini, addestrato per riconoscere sette categorie di scene, compresa una classe dedicata agli elementi sconosciuti. L'addestramento è stato fatto direttamente "sul campo", con un firmware ad hoc che trasmetteva le immagini acquisite dalla fotocamera a un'interfaccia Web e le salvava su una scheda SD.

Il top gamma piu completo? Honor Magic 8 Pro, compralo al miglior prezzo da Aliexpress.com a 802 euro.
